title: Squares, Cubes and Roots
summary: Primes as the building blocks of numbers, square and cube numbers and their surprising patterns, how to find roots, the locker puzzle, and Ramanujan's taxicab number 1729.

ib.statementOfInquiry: Patterns in how numbers are built from primes help us generalize, predict and solve problems about squares, cubes and their roots.

factual: How do we find square roots and cube roots?
Which last digits can a square number have?
conceptual: Why do perfect squares have an odd number of factors?
How does pairing prime factors reveal a square root?
debatable: Is it better to learn divisibility tricks or to understand why they work?
Should calculators be allowed when finding square roots?
